terms.comment: Literally to dig all over (Cato, of the soil); in Sallust, Livy and Suetonius the word for stabbing someone, usually to death. Long ō before nf.
Rare but classical (Lewis & Short). For pricking with a pin or a needle, or a sting.

phrases.latin: vidē nē dolōne collum compungam tibi
phrases.english: mind I don’t prick your neck with my sting
Mind you don’t prick yourself with the needle.

sources: Lewis & Short: confodio · Lewis & Short: compungo
